clue.text: Very keen to get past top of garter

parts.note: something past happened ago, in time gone by

indicators.note: the top of a word is its opening letter, so only the start of garter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone eager to see beyond the top of a stocking's garter.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes someone eagerly excited and impatient to see or hear something.

clue.text: Continental sleeper upset by long wait

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller on a European night train is annoyed by a lengthy delay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reworks LONGWAIT into the answer; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is a sleeping car on a European railway, hence a sleeper on the Continent.

clue.text: Golf club with no front side

indicators.note: having no front means the opening letter of the club's name is dropped

parts.note: a wedge is a golf club with a steeply angled face

explanation.surface: A golfer's club missing its front part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no front' removes the W from WEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: An edge is a side or border of something, as in the edge of a table.

clue.text: Whose publication has a moving letter about TV programme?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the short word for the magazine is read backwards

parts.note: mag is short for magazine, a periodical publication

indicators.note: letters moving about means the word Whose is rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whose magazine carries a touching letter about a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns MAG into GAM, and 'moving letter' rearranges WHOSE into ESHOW; 'has a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A game show is a kind of television programme in which contestants compete for prizes.

clue.text: Ran into camouflaged vessel for what's currently asked at 20

indicators.note: something camouflaged is covered over, so the vessel is concealed within the meeting word

parts.note: to run into someone is to meet them, so ran into gives met
Noah's ark is the crossword's favourite vessel

explanation.surface: A boat disguised as something else bumps into the current asking price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ran into' is a past-tense meeting, not a collision. The definition runs on into 20 across: the going rate a thing would fetch today.
explanation.definitionFit: The market price of goods is the going rate they currently fetch from buyers.

clue.text: Means to spread dough around

parts.note: reads like a rich person's way of spending money, dough being slang for cash, but it is a kitchen tool for flattening pastry dough

explanation.definitionFit: A rolling pin is the kitchen cylinder used to roll pastry dough flat and spread it out.

clue.text: First-class clue spinner

parts.note: a tip is a hint or clue
a top is a toy that spins

explanation.surface: An excellent hint for a spin bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal word for excellent or of the very best quality.

clue.text: Afford the time to sell short before 5

definitions.meaning: to endure or put up with it, finding the patience for it
it goes before 5 down to make a falling market

explanation.surface: A trader finds time to short shares before five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: The 5 refers to 5 down: a BEAR MARKET is one in which prices fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Bear means tolerate or have patience for, and in finance a bear is someone who sells short expecting prices to drop.

clue.text: Amount of money that's taken by English aristocracy on 28

definitions.meaning: slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

definitions.text: that's taken by English aristocracy on 28
definitions.meaning: with 28 down it makes the ... Tour, the European journey young English aristocrats once took

explanation.surface: A sum spent by the English upper classes on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is a thousand units of money, and the Grand Tour was the aristocrat's cultural trip around Europe.

clue.text: -Draw comparisons with a record-breaking flavouring

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open, so the flavouring is broken apart by the other pieces

parts.note: anise is an aniseed flavouring
a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Comparing things with a flavour that sets a new record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record-breaking' reads as one adjective, setting a new best, but splits so that 'breaking' is a container signal working on the flavouring.
explanation.definitionFit: To analogise is to draw an analogy, comparing one thing with another.

clue.text: Pivotal form of impudence after poke from behind

indicators.note: after places the impudence word behind the poking word

parts.note: to goose someone is to poke them in the backside
neck is slang for cheek or impudence

explanation.surface: Someone shows cheek after being prodded in the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A gooseneck is a curved, pivoting fitting, like the bendable arm of a lamp or a boat's boom joint.

clue.text: Subsequently, selling one out during recession

indicators.note: recession means going back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
out means removed, so the one-letter is taken from the selling word

parts.note: retail is the selling of goods to the public
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Later, a shop loses a sale during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' drops I from RETAIL, leaving RETAL, and 'during recession' turns that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means afterwards, at a subsequent time.

clue.text: Big fellow made foolish by a lovelight

indicators.note: made foolish means turned silly and confused, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is O (a zero score in tennis) and light stays as written

explanation.surface: A giant is turned into a fool by the glow of love in someone's eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made foolish' rearranges A, O (love) and LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Goliath was the Philistine giant slain by David, and the name now means any very big man.

clue.text: Nobel-winning author accepts universal principle by 29

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the author's name holds the letter

parts.note: André Gide, the French writer, won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1947
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A prize-winning writer embraces a principle that applies to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts U inside GIDE. The definition joins 29 down: a GUIDELINE is a principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A guideline is a principle or rule meant to direct conduct.

clue.text: Atmosphere on planet's not enough to stop flying officer

parts.note: air is the atmosphere around us
Mars is a planet

indicators.note: not enough means falling short, so the stopping word loses its last letter

parts.note: to halt is to stop

explanation.surface: There isn't enough atmosphere on Mars to halt a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not enough' cuts the T from HALT; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An air marshal is a senior rank of officer in the Royal Air Force.

clue.text: What's seen at end of stay in camp?

definitions.text: What's seen at end of stay in camp?

parts.words: What's seen at end of stay in camp?
parts.note: reads like the close of a holiday at a campsite, but a stay is a guy rope and what sits at its end holds a tent down

explanation.definitionFit: A tent peg is driven into the ground to anchor the guy rope that keeps a tent upright.

clue.text: Scorer that is making a comeback as cricketer

indicators.note: coming back means turning round, so the that-is letters are reversed within the composer's name

parts.note: Edvard Grieg, the Norwegian composer, wrote scores
ie is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A composer reverses that, coming back as a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scorer' looks sporting, as if a run-maker, but means a composer of musical scores. Tony Greig captained England's cricket team in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Greig was a South African-born all-rounder who captained the England cricket side.

clue.text: Bury FC

definitions.meaning: ... Milan is a famous football club, known simply as ...

explanation.definitionFit: Inter means to bury, and Inter is the short name of the Milan football club.

clue.text: Greenback that's part of the bulge on 26 down

definitions.text: that's part of the bulge on 26 down

indicators.note: back means turned round, so the inexperienced word is read backwards

parts.note: green means raw, inexperienced

explanation.surface: A dollar bill that forms part of the bulge in a baby's nappy.
explanation.walkthrough: Greenback looks like a dollar note but splits into Green (RAW) and back. The Battle of the Bulge was in the Second World War; WAR BABY joins 26 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bulge was a battle of the Second World War, so that war is what the battle was part of.

clue.text: Glow of princess almost entering competition

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the shortened name goes into the competition

parts.note: a race is a competition

indicators.note: almost means nearly whole, so the princess's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Diana is a princess, Princess of Wales

explanation.surface: The glow of a princess nearly joining a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes the final letter off the princess's name before it goes into the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiance is a bright glow of light or warmth.

clue.text: Method of choosing diamonds for cutting competition with 18

parts.note: PR is proportional representation, a voting system
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A way of selecting gems for a contest in cutting them.
explanation.walkthrough: With 18 across it makes PRICE WAR, competition by cutting prices.
explanation.definitionFit: A price war is fierce competition in which rival sellers keep cutting prices.

clue.text: A dit is doubly dotty, reportedly

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters are mixed up
doubly means the little word is taken twice over

explanation.surface: A Morse dot sign is said to be twice as dotty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubly' gives IS twice and 'dotty' rearranges A DIT IS IS.
explanation.definitionFit: It is said is a phrase meaning according to what people report.

clue.text: Prefix that's put in organ here

parts.note: en- is a prefix meaning to put in, as in encase
a gland is an organ of the body

explanation.surface: A prefix inserted into a church organ.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here' means the country of the setter and of the Guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: For a British newspaper setter, here is the country where the clue is being written.

clue.text: Little fellow swallows drug for what makes him so

indicators.note: swallows means takes inside, so the little man holds the drug letter

parts.note: a gnome is a little man of folklore
E is short for ecstasy, a drug

explanation.surface: A small man takes a pill to account for his size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts E inside GNOME. The definition points back at the little fellow: his genetic make-up keeps him small.
explanation.definitionFit: The genome is the full set of genes that determines an organism's traits.

clue.text: Algerian governor maintains place for representative

indicators.note: maintains means holds, so the governor holds the placing word

parts.note: the dey was the governor of Algiers under Ottoman rule
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A North African ruler keeps a seat for a delegate.
explanation.walkthrough: The dey ruled Algiers for the Ottomans until 1830, a crossword regular worth remembering.
explanation.definitionFit: A deputy is someone who acts as a representative or substitute for another.

clue.text: Ring round African party to get beastly performer with 8

indicators.note: round means going around, so the ringing sound goes outside the party

parts.note: ding is a ringing sound
the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party

explanation.surface: A bell sounds around an African party with a dancing bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a circle doing the surrounding, but it is the sound of a bell. With 8 down the answer makes a performing animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A dancing bear was an animal trained to perform for crowds.

clue.text: Transport's riding on extra payment

indicators.note: riding means travelling in, so the little word rides inside the vehicle

parts.note: a bus is a means of transport

explanation.surface: A bus rider gets an extra payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' stays as written and is the passenger riding inside the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonus is an extra payment on top of normal wages.

clue.text: Howl about Bach's first instrument when introducing 9

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the howl goes around the letter

parts.note: to bay is to howl like a hound

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A howl about Bach's first instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts B inside BAY. With 9 across it makes BABY GRAND, a small grand piano.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby grand is the smallest kind of grand piano.

clue.text: Spoil salt when stirring in resinous liquid

indicators.note: stirring means mixing up, so the letters of both words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ruining salt while stirring it into resin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when stirring' rearranges SPOILSALT.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastisol is a suspension of PVC particles in a liquid plasticiser, a resinous fluid.

clue.text: Outright disaster as shower around with 13 down

indicators.note: a disaster is a mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: out stays as written and right gives R, its usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A complete calamity when the one showing people round is a guide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outright disaster' reads as a total catastrophe, but 'disaster' rearranges OUT plus R (right). With 13 down the answer makes TOUR GUIDE, one who shows visitors around.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour guide is a person who shows visitors round a place, hence a shower in that sense.

clue.text: Putting point in tale of formulaic steps by 25

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the point goes inside the tale word

parts.note: a tale can be a lie, a made-up story
N is the compass point north

explanation.surface: Putting a point into a formulaic story of steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts N inside LIE. With 25 across it makes LINE DANCING, with its set steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Line dancing is done in rows following a fixed sequence of steps.

clue.text: Pompous crowd opposed fundamental circumstances for Tony's leadership

indicators.note: opposed means facing the other way, so the crowd word is turned round

parts.note: a mob is a crowd

indicators.note: circum-stances means standing around, so the basic word stands around a letter

parts.note: basic means fundamental

indicators.note: leadership is the leading or opening letter of a name

explanation.surface: A pompous crowd opposes Tony Blair's leadership in basic terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circumstances' is read as circum-stances, standing round, so it is a container signal. Tony's leadership gives his first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic means pompous and inflated in speech.

clue.text: Problem afoot when introduction's skipped for wedding

indicators.note: skipping the introduction means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

explanation.surface: A foot problem is ignored at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when introduction's skipped' drops the B from BUNION.
explanation.definitionFit: A union is a marriage, the joining of two people at a wedding.
